rule: S3 Buckets should not be publicly accessible.
recommendation: Enable S3 Block Public Access at the account and bucket levels. Use bucket policies with aws:PrincipalArn conditions and KMS encryption at rest.

rule: Do not allow unrestricted ingress (0.0.0.0/0) on administrative ports.
recommendation: Restrict SSH (port 22) and RDP (port 3389) ingress to specific bastion CIDR blocks, or use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager instead of public ingress.

rule: Avoid using root credentials or wildcard IAM policies.
recommendation: Enforce least-privilege IAM roles with permission boundaries. Use temporary credentials through IAM Identity Center or STS.

rule: Prefer ARM-based Graviton instances for standard workloads.
recommendation: Migrate general-purpose and memory-intensive instances to Graviton (e.g. m7g, c7g, r7g) to achieve up to 40% better price-performance compared to x86 equivalents.

rule: Eliminate redundant NAT Gateway data transfer fees.
recommendation: Use VPC Endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) for S3, DynamoDB, and internal AWS services instead of routing traffic out through expensive NAT Gateways.

rule: Choose appropriate capacity mode based on traffic predictability.
recommendation: Use On-Demand capacity for unpredictable or intermittent workloads. Switch to Provisioned capacity with Auto Scaling for predictable baseline workloads with Savings Plans / Reserved Capacity.

rule: Production databases should have Multi-AZ deployment enabled.
recommendation: Enable Multi-AZ replication to allow automated failover without manual intervention. Implement automated snapshots and point-in-time recovery.

rule: Workloads must span across at least two Availability Zones.
recommendation: Configure Auto Scaling Groups with subnets spanning multiple AZs behind an Application Load Balancer with health checks.
